Background.text: Although first sighted by an English navigator in 1592, the first landing (English) did not occur until almost a century later in 1690, and the first settlement (French) was not established until 1764. The colony was turned over to Spain two years later, and the islands have since been the subject of a territorial dispute, first between Britain and Spain, then between Britain and Argentina. The UK asserted its claim to the islands by establishing a naval garrison there in 1833. Argentina invaded the islands in 1982. The British responded with an expeditionary force and after fierce fighting forced an Argentine surrender on 14 June 1982. With hostilities ended and Argentine forces withdrawn, UK administration resumed. In response to renewed calls from Argentina for Britain to relinquish control of the islands, a referendum was held in 2013 that resulted in 99.8% of the population voting to remain a part of the UK.

Location.text: Southern South America, islands in the South Atlantic Ocean, about 500 km east of southern Argentina

Area.note: note: includes the two main islands of East and West Falkland and about 200 small islands

Climate.text: cold marine; strong westerly winds, cloudy, humid; rain occurs on more than half of days in year; average annual rainfall is 60 cm in Stanley; occasional snow all year, except in January and February, but typically does not accumulate

Terrain.text: rocky, hilly, mountainous with some boggy, undulating plains

Natural resources.text: fish, squid, wildlife, calcified seaweed, sphagnum moss

Natural hazards.text: strong winds persist throughout the year

Geography - note.text: deeply indented coast provides good natural harbors; short growing season

Population.note: note: data include all persons usually resident in the islands at the time of the 2021 census

Ethnic groups.text: Falkland Islander 48.3%, British 23.1%, St. Helenian 7.5%, Chilean 4.6%, mixed 6%, other 8.5%, unspecified 2% (2016 est.)

Population distribution.text: a very small population, with most residents living in and around Stanley

Economic overview.text: British South American territorial economy; longstanding fishing industry; surging tourism prior to COVID-19 and Brexit; recent offshore hydrocarbon discoveries threaten ecotourism industries; no central bank and must have British approval on currency shifts

Agricultural products.text: fodder and vegetable crops; venison, sheep, dairy products; fish, squid

Exports - commodities.text: shellfish, fish, wool, sheep and goat meat (2023)
